summary: Batch campaigns recorded a submission only after the scheduler call and took no lock, so an interrupted or concurrent submit could send the same chunks twice; the default merge concatenated string results silently.

database_specific.introduced_basis: the root commit of the repository history (the 0.3.0 import) already has the defect; releases before 0.3.0 are not in this history
database_specific.fixed_basis: fixed in 0.4.0 (CHANGELOG 0.4.0; release commit 9870a35 holds the fix); 0.4.0 has no tag and no release manifest

observables: merged result and submission record of a partitioned batch campaign (core/partition)
impact.bias: jobs could run at the scheduler without a campaign record (a kill after executor.submit() returned), and the next submit sent the same chunks again; two concurrent submits shared a submission ID (len(submissions), no lock); the default merge concatenated string results instead of refusing them, and did not refuse NaN, infinite or overflowed values
impact.trigger: a submit interrupted after the scheduler accepted the jobs, two submits of one campaign at once, or chunk results that are strings or non-finite

outputs.how_to_recognize: local_partition.py merge report (JSON on stdout); only batch_campaign.py writes a computational-run, naming the tool 'hep-research core/partition runner'

remedy: for a run made with a core/partition campaign in this range: check the scheduler accounting for chunks submitted twice and merge again with a release that has the fix; runs not made with a campaign are not affected (the scan lists every computational-run of the range: the artifact does not record whether a campaign was used)
